Mr. President, members of the Security Council, I thank you for the opportunity to address the Council on the longstanding cooperation between the United Nations and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in maintaining international peace and security. At a time of growing geopolitical complexity, cooperation with regional and sub-regional organizations such as the OIC remains indispensable. Guided by Chapter VIII of the Charter, such cooperation is a key priority of the Secretary-General and an important part of implementing the Pact for the future. The OSCE brings together 57 member states and represents a vital political, economic, cultural, and religious constituency. Its voice carries considerable weight in some of the world's conflict-affected situations. The United Nations values this partnership not only as a matter of institutional cooperation, but as an essential component of our efforts to promote durable peace, inclusive governance, and respect for international human rights law. The United Nations-OIC cooperation spans a broad range of country-specific and thematic areas. The biennial UN-OIC General Cooperation Meeting, mandated by the General Assembly, serves as a vital platform, bringing together senior representatives of our 2 organizations to take stock of our cooperation, and discuss ways to enhance it strategically. In the context of today's complex geopolitical landscape and challenging financial environment, this meeting assumes increased relevance and urgency. Mr. President, in the Middle East, the United Nations and the OIC have long shared common objectives in seeking a lasting and comprehensive resolution to the question of Palestine. Most recently, the United Nations and the OIC organized the annual Joint Conference on the Question of Jerusalem, held in Dakar on July 9th. The United Nations also appreciates the OIC and the League of Arab States for endorsing the Recovery and Reconstruction Plan for Gaza through their Joint Ministerial Committee. This plan reinforces the collective push for a just and comprehensive solution rooted in relevant United Nations resolutions. The upcoming Ministerial Meeting to Support the Two-State Solution, co-chaired by France and Saudi Arabia, is key to highlighting international consensus around these goals and reaffirming the principles sustaining the two-state solution. In Lebanon, the United Nations maintains regular engagement with the OIC, in support of the country's stability. Amid recent regional tensions, the OIC's consistent political backing for Lebanon has proven particularly valuable. In Afghanistan, the OIC is a key partner in our efforts for a coherent and structured engagement with the de facto authorities in the framework of the UN-convened Doha process. The OSCE has also played an important role in supporting the human rights of Afghan women and girls through dialogue with the de facto authorities, drawing on its unique position as the collective and credible voice of the Muslim world. The OSCE is also a vital leading voice in support of the Rohingya, highlighting the need to address the root causes of their displacement and to create conditions for their safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable return to Myanmar, including the right to citizenship. The United Nations welcomes the continued coordination between the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General on Myanmar and the OIC in pursuit of shared objectives. In Sudan, after more than 2 years of relentless fighting, the warring parties continue to pursue military gains. The OIC's support to international mediation efforts, including those of Personal Envoy Lamamra, remains highly valuable as efforts continue to find resolution that will prevent further disaster and return Sudan to a path of peace. The United Nations welcomes the ceasefire between Israel and Iran continues to hold. All international actors should speak with one voice in impressing upon the 2 countries to adhere to the ceasefire. The OSCE resolution on Iran made at the 51st session of its Council of Ministers last month in Istanbul to establish an open-ended ministerial contact group on de-escalation to work toward the peaceful settlement of the conflict is a valuable contribution to international and UN efforts in this regard.

Thank you.

Across contexts such as the Sahel, Syria, and Yemen, OIC Member States have lent important support to UN efforts to advance peace and security. Mr. President, we appreciate the OIC's cooperation in addressing global challenges that transcend borders. As Islamophobia continues to affect far too many people around the world, and demands attention. The United Nations stands against all forms of hatred and discrimination and firmly believes that diversity in all its forms only makes societies stronger. The Secretary-General's recent appointment of Mr. Mirgil Moratinos, a Special Envoy to Combat Islamophobia, reflects the United Nations' determination to intensify efforts on this important issue in cooperation with the OSCE and other partners. The United Nations and the OSCE also cooperate on electoral matters. Through their longstanding and active partnership in this area, we have jointly implemented several capacity development initiatives in recent years. These have included co-organizing trainings on election observation and promoting women's participation in electoral and political processes for OIC member states. Our partnership has also included staff exchange programs aimed at strengthening cooperation and sharing of experiences and good practices on electoral matters. Our joint efforts in countering terrorism and preventing violent extremism continue to develop. Following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding in March 2024, the United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism and the OIC have advanced rights-based approaches through technical assistance, parliamentary engagement, and strategic dialogue. Mr. President, in a world beset by interconnected challenges that continue to grow and multiply, We must pursue every advantage and leverage every instrument we have at our disposal to deliver meaningful and lasting impact, consistent with our shared commitment to peace and security. By joining forces, the United Nations and the OIC are helping to reinvigorate multilateralism and restore trust in our institutions. As we move forward with the implementation of the Pact of the Future, the United Nations-OIC partnership will remain critical to defuse tensions, advance sustainable peace, reinforce multilateral norms and principles, and promote equitable and sustainable development. Thank you.

I shall now make a statement in my capacity as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Excellencies, distinguished colleagues, it is a distinct honor for me to preside over today's meeting of the Security Council on the cooperation between the United Nations and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, known as OIC, a subject that resonates profoundly with our multilateral vision and with the collective aspirations of the over 1.9 billion people whom the OIC represents. I thank the OIC Assistant Secretary-General, Mr. Yusuf Al-Dubai, for traveling from Jeddah to brief the Council. I also thank Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khayari for his valuable briefing. We meet at a moment of deepening global disorder. Wars waged with impunity, occupation sustained without accountability, humanitarian crises multiplying, and ideologies of hatred fast becoming normalized. Amidst prevailing flux and deepening uncertainty, the urgency for coordination and principled action has never been greater. Pakistan firmly believes that in this fractured world, the OIC stands as a key political actor, and its partnership with the United Nations must be strengthened, deepened, and further institutionalized. The cooperation between the United Nations and the OIC is firmly based on Chapter 8 of the UN Charter, which highlights the significance of regional arrangements in supporting the Security Council's primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. As the second-largest intergovernmental organization after the UN, the OSCE has consistently served as a bridge connecting the global with regional efforts and aligning political with humanitarian priorities. Its legitimacy derives not only from its vast and diverse membership, but from the principled clarity of its mandate to uphold justice, protect human dignity, respect national sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of all member states, and advance solidarity among nations. Whether in championing the rights of the Palestinian people, for freedom and statehood, in advancing for the rights of the people of Jammu and Kashmir for self-determination, an end to the prolonged illegally occupied occupation by India, or in supporting peace efforts across Libya, Afghanistan, Syria, Yemen, and Sahel and beyond, the OSCE has been an indispensable interlocutor for the United Nations also deeply attached to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. Pakistan holds this partnership in the highest regard. As a founding member of the OIC and a staunch believer in effective multilateralism, we are of the view that this engagement must transcend and evolve into operational synergy. That means early warning systems informed background realities, joint mediation frameworks built on trust, and sustained political and technical collaboration that delivers tangible impact on the ground. Excellencies, the General Assembly, during its 79th session, adopted Resolution 79/9, reaffirming the relevance of the UN-OIC partnership and calling for stronger institutional linkages and strategic cooperation. The OIC's regional presence, cultural sensitivity, and political legitimacy allow it to respond swiftly and credibly, especially in contexts where global mechanisms are constrained or absent. The depth of the UN-OIC engagement continues to grow, from mediation in political transition to coordinated responses in humanitarian emergency to advocacy on issues of disarmament, development, and protection of religious and cultural heritage. This progressive transformation into a proactive, multi-dimensional partnership underscores the maturity and scope of this relationship. The potential of institutional linkage remains much more in this regard. Excellencies, nowhere is this cooperation more necessary than in, in countering the rising tide of extreme extremism, particularly the alarming resurgence of Islamophobia. Religious hatred is not only morally indefensible, indefensible, it strikes at the very foundation of the UN Charter. The international community's endorsement of Pakistan's initiative to designate 15th of March as the International Day to Combat Islamophobia, followed by the adoption of a resolution leading to the appointment of a UN Special Envoy on Islamophobia, are milestones that reaffirm our shared resolve. The OIC has long been a strong voice on this issue, and we must further institutionalize its role in global efforts to promote respect, inclusion, and interfaith harmony. Excellencies, today's interaction is both timely and necessary. Let us recall that this Council has convened briefings on UN-OIC cooperation in 2013, and 2016, and adopted a Presidential Statement in 2013 recognizing the OSCE's constructive role. We must embed this cooperation in regular, durable, and structured mechanisms— mechanisms that reflect mutual trust, institutional coherence, and a genuine commitment to shared responsibility. The OIC is a vital partner in the international peace and security architecture, particularly in theatres where the UN's reach alone has proven insufficient. Similarly, on the important issue of UN Security Council reform, as the largest cross-regional organization, the OIC Member States have called for adequate representation in any category of an expanded Security Council, in line with the OIC's long-held position. Excellencies, Pakistan hopes that today's dialogue will be a catalyst for fresh thinking, renewed commitment, and bold action. Let us be guided by the Charter, grounded in principles, not geopolitics, and propelled by the conviction that global challenges demand global partnerships. Cooperation between the United Nations and the regional organizations such as the OSC is not a diplomatic accessory. It is an indispensable imperative. Excellencies, before I conclude, I wish to thank all delegations for their constructive engagement in agreeing on a presidential statement to be adopted at this meeting that will go a long way in further strengthening the partnership of cooperation between the United Nations and the OIC. I thank you all. I now resume my functions as President of the Council, and I'm happy to give the floor to the representative of Guyana.

As members of both organizations, Guyana reiterates our support and commitment to the strengthening of cooperation between the UN and the OIC to foster viable solutions for a more peaceful world. I thank you.

Children should be able to grow up free from fear and safe from violence. Every person, no matter their faith or ethnicity, should be able to enjoy a life of dignity and hope. Unfortunately, war and terrorism have limited the opportunities of some people to enjoy the safety and prosperity to which we all aspire. There are countless crises and challenges that regularly come before this Council, which affect the lives and livelihoods of people across the member states of the OIC. Examples include the catastrophic war in Sudan that is the cause of the world's largest humanitarian crisis, the violence and blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by terrorist groups in Mali and the region, and the actions of the Houthis that endanger the lives of seafarers and harm economies across the region. In the face of these crises, we encourage the OIC and its member states to use their good offices to resolve tensions and conflicts and strive for peace. We welcome OIC member states' sharing of valuable experiences in countering terrorism and violent extremism. For example, the successes of some OIC members in repatriating, reintegrating, and rehabilitating individuals susceptible to violent extremist ideology can benefit other OIC member states and the international community more broadly. We encourage the OIC and its member states to be a force for cooperation and reconciliation across religious and national lines. This includes supporting Muslim groups facing repression, conflict, and humanitarian crises outside of the OIC, such as Uyghurs in China and/or Rohingya in Myanmar and beyond Myanmar's borders. We would appreciate your sustained engagement with Beijing over the treatment of your fellow Muslims in China. We welcome your efforts to bridge religious divides and encourage the normalization of ties with Israel. We have already seen countries who signed the Abraham Accords benefit from increased security and prosperity. The United States and OIC member states have a common interest in enhancing regional and international security and growing our economies. We look forward to continuing our work with the OIC member states to deter threats and advance peace, stability, and prosperity throughout the world. We hope that greater cooperation between the UN and OIC can advance those goals. I thank you.
Thank you, Representative of United States, for the statement. I now give the floor to the Representative of United Kingdom.

Thank you, President, and I'd like to add my thanks to our distinguished briefers, ASG Khiari and ASG Aldobe. Thank you. I welcome the opportunity today to discuss the OIC's important cooperation with the UN on the resolution of conflicts and securing lasting peace and prosperity. I'll make 3 points, President. First, the United Kingdom welcomes the efforts of the OIC to strengthen its role in conflict prevention, confidence-building, peacekeeping, and mediation. In particular, we thank OIC members for their invaluable commitment of troops to UN peacekeeping operations. Effective cooperation and sharing of information between the UN and OIC is important for developing coherent strategies for Conflict Prevention to support national prevention efforts. Second, the United Kingdom values the role of the OIC and its member states as a key partner in our shared fight against terrorism and violent extremism. This requires a multidimensional approach with the support of all relevant UN agencies, regional organizations, governments, and civil society partners. We encourage the UN and the OIC to maintain close coordination to ensure the protection of human rights while countering terrorism. Third, the United Kingdom welcomes its broadening and deepening relationship with the OIC and its members. Including this week hosting the OIC's International Academy of Jurisprudence to strengthen collaboration on key issues and interfaith dialogue. We value this collaboration not least because inclusive governance and respect for human rights are fundamental underpinnings of peace and prosperity. And the United Kingdom firmly believes the rights to freedom of religion or belief and to freedom of expression have a crucial role to play in this regard. Religious intolerance and persecution fuel instability, impeding both conflict prevention and resolution, as we sadly see in a number of the conflicts on this Council's agenda. That is why the United Kingdom was proud to co-pen Security Council Resolution 2686 with the United Arab Emirates in 2023. This was the first time a Security Council resolution had directly addressed the persecution of religious minorities in conflict settings. We remain committed to the full implementation of Resolution 2686. In conclusion, President, when freedom of religion or belief and freedom of expression are respected for all and interreligious dialogue is promoted, we can build trust and understanding between communities, helping to secure sustainable peace. I thank you.
Thank you, Representative of United Kingdom, for the statement. I will now give the floor to Representative of Sierra Leone.

Thank you, Mr. President, and also thank you, SG Kerry and Assistant Secretary-General Aldebaran, for their valuable briefings. Sierra Leone reaffirms that cooperation between the United Nations and regional and sub-regional organizations as envisaged in Chapter 8 of the UN Charter, is indispensable in the maintenance of international peace and security. In this context, we underscore the relevance and unique positioning of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, or the OIC, which through its cultural, historical, and political ties with member states has a crucial role in preventing, mediating, and resolving conflicts in various regions. Sierra Leone believes deeply in the power of multilateral diplomacy and regional partnerships. We therefore fully support closer coordination between the UN and the OIC in conflict prevention, humanitarian response, and peacebuilding, particularly in regions experiencing persistent instability and fragility. Specifically, we fully support closer coordination between the United Nations and the OIC in conflict prevention, humanitarian response, and peacebuilding, particularly in regions experiencing protracted crisis, fragility, and instability. We commend the OSCE's proactive engagement in supporting cessation of hostilities, promoting inclusive political dialogue, and facilitating diplomatic initiatives aimed at resolving conflict. The OSCE's efforts to work in complementarity with regional and international actors, including the African Union and the Secretary-General's Envoys, are essential to achieving durable and locally owned solutions. We also acknowledge the OIC's role in addressing humanitarian emergencies. Its efforts to facilitate humanitarian access, support early recovery, and advocacy for the protection of civilians are vital. We encourage deeper collaboration between the OIC and United Nations humanitarian agencies to scale up life-saving assistance and promote principled humanitarian action grounded in international law. Furthermore, OIC's support for inclusive political processes and national reconciliation remains critical to the success of peacebuilding initiatives. We call for sustained engagement to strengthen democratic governance, foster credible and inclusive political transitions, and build the foundations for long-term stability and peace. We recognize the opportunities presented by increased OSCE engagement in regions undergoing transition. Its continued involvement in advancing national dialogue, promoting unity, and supporting the reintegration of marginalized communities will contribute meaningfully to inclusive and sustainable peace. Mr. President, for the UN-OIC partnership to reach its full potential, 3 areas require further attention. First, greater technical and financial support is needed to address the OIC's capacity limitations in conflict mediation and peacebuilding. Second, more deliberate alignment of conflict analysis and early warning mechanisms between the UN and the OSCE could prevent escalation and enhance response readiness. Third, increased joint initiatives in intercultural and interfaith dialogue are essential to counter anti-Muslim hatred, violent extremism, and sectarianism. Sierra Leone supports the continued implementation of the UN General Assembly Resolution on OIC-UN-OIC cooperation and encourages periodic joint assessments and policy dialogues between both organizations. Furthermore, we believe that promoting a culture of peace must remain central to our multilateral peace and security agenda. As such, the United Nations Alliance of Civilizations in coordination with the OSCE, can serve as an effective platform for advancing intercultural understanding, religious tolerance, and the inclusion of youth and women in peace processes. The OSCE, with its broad and diverse membership across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, is well-suited to lead grassroots efforts in this regard. In conclusion, we reiterate our firm belief that strengthening the cooperation between the United Nations and the OSCE will not only boost regional responses to conflict, but will enhance the legitimacy and effectiveness of global efforts to address the root causes of instability, foster reconciliation, and promote a just and enduring peace. Thank you.
Thank you, Representative of Sierra Leone. Now I will give the floor to Representative of Republic of Korea.

These include extreme weather events, floods, and drought on the African continent, which are all crisis multipliers. It has also made investments in economic development and infrastructure. Playing an important role in post-crisis recovery and resilience building. In the Middle East, since the horrendous terrorist attack by Hamas on October 7th, 2023, and the following harsh military response, we have been witnessing dangerous escalation and instability spreading throughout the region. Je remercie Monsieur le Président, Votre Excellence Mohamed Ishaq Dar. La France salue le Pakistan pour avoir pris l'initiative de cette réunion. Je remercie Monsieur le Sous-Sécrétaire général pour le Moyen-Orient, l'Asie et le Pacifique, Monsieur Khaled ainsi que Monsieur le Secrétaire général adjoint aux Affaires politiques de l'Organisation de la coopération islamique, Monsieur Youssef Al-Dobey, pour leurs interventions. Ces interventions ont mis en évidence des points de convergence entre les actions de l'OCI et les buts et principes des Nations unies, notamment leurs objectifs communs que sont le maintien de la paix, la résolution pacifique des différends ou la promotion de la coopération multilatérale. Nous nous félicitons de l'engagement pris par l'OCI de continuer à œuvrer à la paix et à la sécurité internationale dans le respect du cadre fixé par le droit international, en particulier par les résolutions du Conseil de sécurité. Nous souhaiterions mettre en avant deux thèmes sur lesquels l'OCI peut contribuer à la réalisation des buts et principes des Nations unies. Tout d'abord, la résolution des crises qui touchent les membres de l'OCI. Plusieurs pays de l'OCI sont touchés par le terrorisme. L'Organisation de la coopération islamique a de longue date fait de la lutte contre ce fléau l'une de ses priorités, en adoptant et mettant régulièrement à jour sa Convention sur la lutte contre le terrorisme international. À l'heure de la recrudescence et de la mutation de la menace terroriste, nous appelons l'organisation à poursuivre ses efforts dans le respect constant des droits de l'homme et des résolutions pertinentes du Conseil de sécurité. Sur la situation au Proche-Orient, alors que la conférence sur la solution à deux États que la France copréside avec l'Arabie saoudite se tiendra la semaine prochaine, nous nous félicitons de voir l'OCI soutenir ce chemin vers la paix et la sécurité pour tous sur la base des deux États. Nous sommes enfin convaincus que l'OCI, au sein de laquelle la Syrie vient de retrouver sa place après des années de guerre, qu'elle a traversée peut jouer un rôle dans le rétablissement de la paix civile et la réintégration du pays au sein de la communauté internationale et contribuer au relèvement socio-économique de la Syrie, notamment à travers la Banque islamique de développement. L'OCI peut faire entendre une voix forte en faveur du dialogue intercommunautaire et de la protection de tous les civils, en soutien aux autorités de transition de Damas. De manière générale, l'OCI joue un rôle bienvenu dans l'assistance humanitaire des populations qui en ont besoin. La contribution militaire, par ailleurs, des membres de l'OCI aux opérations de maintien de la paix est également à souligner. La réponse aux défis transversaux est un autre sujet sur lequel l'OCI peut apporter son concours. Le changement climatique, en particulier, exacerbe les vulnérabilités. Dans les territoires des pays membres de l'OCI, la désertification, l'augmentation des sécheresses et l'accroissement de l'insécurité hydrique sont une réalité préoccupante. Les atténuer et s'y adapter sont une nécessité pour favoriser la stabilité régionale. L'OCI peut faire la différence en en faisant une priorité de son action. Ensuite, nous estimons que l'OCI a tout son rôle à jouer pour développer et encourager le respect des droits de l'homme et des libertés fondamentales pour tous, sans distinction d'origine, de sexe, de langue ou de religion. Nous encourageons ainsi l'organisation à poursuivre sa contribution à la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes et les discriminations de genre via des programmes comme le plan d'action de l'OCI pour les femmes. En Afghanistan, où la dégradation du sort des femmes et des petites filles doit continuer de mobiliser toute notre attention, nous sommes convaincus que l'OCI peut être un important relais de l'action de l'ONU et du Conseil de sécurité. Monsieur le Président, d'autres défis globaux pourraient être évoqués, comme la lutte contre la désinformation, la gouvernance de l'internet, l'éducation ou la santé. Pour relever tous ces défis globaux auxquels l'OCI est également confrontée, comme le reste de la communauté internationale, aucune méthode n'est plus éprouvée

I thank the representative of Algeria for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Greece.

Thank you, Mr. President, and let me thank ASG Hiari and Mr. Yusuf al-Dubai, Assistant Secretary General. of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation for their briefings. Greece very much welcomes today's opportunity to exchange views on the cooperation between the United Nations and the OIC in accordance with the UN Charter and its Chapter 8 provisions. Today, I would like to highlight the following 3 points. First, Greece reaffirms its support for enhanced cooperation between the UN and regional and sub-regional organizations in accordance with Chapter 8 of the UN Charter. Regional organizations have a valuable role to play in promoting regional and, by extension, international peace and security. They can be suitably placed to foster dialogue and facilitate regional solutions to challenges which often exceed the regional scope. We highly value the contribution of such organizations to the peaceful settlement of disputes, as well as their ability to complement the work of the United Nations. Provided that their conduct remains fully consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN, its Charter, and the resolutions of the Security Council, they can serve as important platforms for conflict prevention, preventive diplomacy, reconciliation and peacebuilding, to name a few. In this spirit, Greece encourages the continued dialogue and structured cooperation between the UN and regional organizations, stressing the need for their conduct to be fully aligned with international law and Security Council resolutions. Second, Greece supports constructive engagement between the UN and the OIC towards the fulfillment of UN principles and purposes. The engagement between the UN and the OIC, a cross-regional faith-based organization, particularly in conflict-affected regions such as the Middle East, North Africa, and the Sahel, has the potential to demonstrate the value of regional perspectives in multilateral diplomacy. Enjoying strong bilateral ties with many of its members, Greece additionally acknowledges the active role of current States members to the OIC serving on the Security Council, with which we enjoy excellent cooperation. Third, Greece expresses its serious concern of and opposition to the content of certain resolutions adopted by the OIC, as well as elements in its declarations which contravene international law, the UN Charter, and Security Council resolutions. Greece underscores that OIC resolutions must always be fully aligned with the international law, the UN Charter, and the resolutions of the Security Council, namely on issues pertaining to the Cyprus issue, and the non-interference in the domestic affairs of sovereign States, according to Article 2, paragraph 7 of the United Nations Charter. With regard to the Cyprus issue, Greece emphasizes the need for strict adherence to Security Council Resolutions 541 and 550. The OIC has most regrettably attributed observer status to the secessionist entity on the island, since 2004. This, despite the fact that the Security Council, with its resolutions 541 and 550, clearly condemned its unilateral declaration of independence, demanding it be withdrawn. It equally called upon all states to respect the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the Republic of Cyprus and not to recognize the illegal entity or assist it in any way. In addition, OIC resolutions and elements in its declarations outright contravene international law. In fact, the OIC's latest ministerial summit joint declaration speaks of a so-called Turkish Muslim minority of Western Thrace, as well as the Turkish Muslim population in the Dodecanese. Any such reference is factually incorrect, as the International Treaty of Lausanne established the status of the Muslim minority in Thrace, Greece, on the basis of religion. Likewise, the small population of Greek citizens of Muslim faith residing in the islands of Rhodes and Kos in the Dodecanese enjoy the same rights as any other Greek citizen, with their religious rights and freedoms fully protected. Mr. President, we regret that past efforts to raise these concerns with OIC Secretariat have not borne fruit. We hope today's exchange offers a fresh opportunity to reaffirm the importance of aligning all regional positions with international law and Security Council resolutions. At the end of the day, adopting positions that blatantly contravene international law does little to advance cooperation with the United Nations or contribute to the work of the Security Council. Thank you, Mr. President. Allow me to begin by expressing our sincere gratitude to the Pakistani presidency for convening this meeting and for the thoughtful decision to place the vital partnership between the United Nations and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation at the center of the Council's agenda today. I also like to thank our esteemed briefers, Mr. Khaled Khayyari, Assistant Secretary-General for Middle East and Asia-Pacific, and Mr. Youssef Al-Dubai, Assistant Secretary-General for Political Affairs of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, for their valuable insights and assessments. As a founding member of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, my delegation attaches great importance to the enduring partnership between the UN and the OIC. Over the years, this relationship has proven itself to be a valuable asset in our collective efforts to maintain international peace and security. Drawing on the OIC's regional legitimacy and the UN's global mandate, we have together addressed a range of challenges, from conflict prevention and mediation to humanitarian aid delivery and post-conflict recovery. Collaborative work in regions such as the Middle East North Africa and the Sahel has demonstrated the practical value of this partnership. Yet we live in a world where threats are evolving rapidly, conflicts can ignite overnight, and narratives of division can spread in an instant. To remain effective, This partnership must not only continue, but be revitalized and reimagined. I wish to offer 3 points for consideration as we seek to further strengthen this cooperation. First, there is scope to enhance joint preventative diplomacy. The UN and the OIC can work jointly on addressing the root causes of conflicts and improve conflict prevention efforts, including strengthening early warning systems and supporting mediation. Leveraging the OIC's regional knowledge and expertise with the UN's global reach makes early intervention more proactive and effective. Second, institutionalizing collaboration should be a priority. Continue to work towards stronger relationships, such as through joint working groups, capacity-building programs, and coordinated approaches to peacekeeping, will create a more systematic and sustained partnership. Third, we must continue to promote intercultural and interfaith dialogue, leveraging innovation and technology to broaden our reach and deepen our impact. Harnessing artificial intelligence, digital communication platforms, and innovative educational tools can counter divisive narratives more effectively. Additionally, adopting technological solutions to bridge cultural and religious divides can reinforce the foundation of lasting peace and inclusivity at all levels of society. To conclude, Mr. President, the UN and the OIC share a commitment to the purposes and the principles of the UN Charter. My delegation remains committed to strengthening the partnership between the United Nations and the OIC, and to meet the challenges ahead more effectively as we advance our shared aspirations for peace and security around the world. I thank you.

Excellencies, dear colleagues, after consultations among Council members, I have been authorized to make the following statement on their behalf. I quote: The Security Council recalls the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations and reaffirms its primary responsibility under the Charter for the maintenance of international peace and security. And in this regard, the Security Council reiterates that cooperation between the United Nations and regional and sub-regional organizations and arrangements in matters relating to the maintenance of international peace and security, and consistent with Chapter 8 of the Charter of the United Nations, can improve collective security. This— the Security Council recalls its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President, which underscores the importance of developing effective partnerships between the United Nations and the regional and sub-regional organizations, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and the relevant statutes of the regional and sub-regional organizations. The Security Council expresses its appreciation for the briefings of the Assistant Secretary-General of the United Nations, Mr. Khaled Khayyari, and the Assistant Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, Mr. Yusuf al-Dubai. The Security Council takes note of the 16th Biennial General Meeting of the Organization and Agencies of the United Nations System and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and its subsidiary organs and specialized and affiliated institutions held in Astana from 22nd to 24th of July 2024 to review and appraise the level of cooperation between the 2 organizations and acknowledges the value of further strengthening cooperation in areas of common interest. The Security Council notes the United Nations and the regional and sub-regional organizations, including the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, work in promoting and facilitating the resolution of conflicts and stressed the need for this work to be consistent with the Charter of the United Nations and the relevant resolutions of the Security Council. The Security Council reaffirms its commitment to the pacific settlement of disputes in conformity with the Charter of the United Nations, in particular Chapter 6. The Security Council notes the interest of utilizing the existing and potential capabilities of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in this regard, including through encouraging its member countries to resolve differences peacefully through dialogue, reconciliation, consultation, negotiation, good offices, mediation, and judicial settlement of dispute. The Security Council recognizes the important role of the good offices of the Secretary-General and encourages the Secretary-General to continue to use mediation as often as possible to help resolve conflicts peacefully, working in close coordination with the OIC in that regard as appropriate. The Security Council welcomes the efforts of the OIC, which have been undertaken in coordination with the United Nations, in strengthening its role in the conflict prevention, confidence, confidence building, peacekeeping, conflict resolution, and post-conflict rehabilitation, mediation, and preventive diplomacy, and stresses the need for this work to be consistent with the UN Charter and relevant resolutions of the Council. The Security Council recognizes the importance of interaction and cooperation where appropriate, between the Peacebuilding Commission and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in support of nationally owned and inclusive peacebuilding efforts. The Council commends the Member States of the OIC for their ongoing commitment to international peacekeeping and peacebuilding, including through the contribution of troops to the United Nations peacekeeping operations. The Security Council recognizes the value of close cooperation as appropriate with regional and sub-regional organizations, including the OIC, in order to enhance the implementation of the United Nations Security Council resolutions in a coherent, efficient, and effective manner. The Security Council notes that sharing of information and analysis between the UN And the OIC is relevant for advancing their shared concerns on conflict prevention, conflict resolution, and peacebuilding, and encourages exploring further cooperation in this area. The Security Council commends the commitment of the OIC to building its capacity in the field of conflict prevention and resolution, mediation, and preventive diplomacy. The Security Council recognizes the relevance of enhancing cooperation with the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in the maintenance of international peace and security and expresses its intention to hold regular briefings of the Security Council as appropriate in this regard. The Security Council requests the Secretary-General to include in his next biannual report to the Security Council and the General Assembly on cooperation between the United Nations and regional and other organizations, recommendations on ways to further enhance cooperation between the United Nations and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. This statement will be issued as a document of the Security Council Under the symbol S/PRST/2025/5. There are no names inscribed on the list of speakers. The meeting stands adjourned.
